latitude.why: Exec semantics (direct exec vs typed into a shell), how a commanded window interacts with session adoption, parser choice, and dir-flag spelling are reviewer-debatable; desktop keys and app-id plumbing are forced.

q1.position: Accept `-e`; remaining argv is the command. TD spawns the user's shell in the pane, shell-escapes the argv, and types the line into the PTY — the exact mechanism new_restored uses for TD_SEED_RESUME.
q1.rationale: Reuses the proven resume path; when the agent exits the user keeps a live shell instead of a vanished window.

q2.position: Parse `--app-id=<id>` (= or space form) and plumb it into WindowOptions.app_id at cx.open_window, replacing the hard-coded "terminal-delight"; absent flag keeps the default.
q2.rationale: app_id set before the window maps, so compositor rules match on first map — no post-open set_app_id race.

q3.position: `--working-directory=<dir>` (foot's spelling) becomes the seed cwd — session::PaneRestore.cwd into term::spawn_in(cwd), the same plumbing TD_SEED_CWD uses; a vanished dir falls back safely.
q3.rationale: spawn_in(cwd) exists; foot-parity spelling also serves callers that bypass xdg-terminal-exec with foot-shaped args.

q4.position: `--title=<t>` overrides window_title() in TitlebarOptions at open; declared to consumers as X-TerminalArgTitle=--title= in packaging/terminal-delight.desktop.
q4.rationale: Title already flows through TitlebarOptions; the desktop key is where xdg-terminal-exec learns the flag.

q5.position: Add exactly four keys to packaging/terminal-delight.desktop: X-TerminalArgExec=-e, X-TerminalArgAppId=--app-id=, X-TerminalArgTitle=--title=, X-TerminalArgDir=--working-directory=. Every existing key stays.
q5.rationale: Mirrors omarchy's shipped foot.desktop — the exact contract omarchy-launch-tui and xdg-terminal-exec consume.

q6.position: Unchanged: a bare launch adopts the most-recently-saved unheld session and restores it (instance::resolve_session); flag_reply still answers --help/--version and refuses unknown flags without opening a window.
q6.rationale: Existing behaviour is tested and deliberate; the ticket adds surface, it must not change the default.

q7.position: Hand-rolled: a small parse_launch_args() in main.rs, run after the verb dispatch and ahead of flag_reply so the new flags aren't refused; no new crate.
q7.rationale: The repo has zero arg-crate deps by design; four flags plus terminal -e don't justify one.

q8.position: A commanded window never adopts an existing saved session, but it claims a FRESH session id and persists like a normal window — its typed command line is recorded, so crash recovery reopens the agent.
q8.rationale: The session-recovery machinery exists so agent panes survive crashes; scratch would exempt every `omarchy agent` window from it.
